chapter: Los Angeles, Ellington and the recording scene
title: The Black and White musicians' locals in Los Angeles
summary: Elmer Fain was business agent; Local 767 was the Black local and 747 the White, with Lester Young's family living beside the Black local.

blocks.x: You were mentioning Elmer Fain. What was his function at that time? Now he's a business agent of the...
He was a business agent at that point.

At that time there were two locals, a Black local and a White local. 767 was the Black local and 747 was the White local. The White local was located on Georgia Street in downtown Los Angeles, and the Black local was on Central Avenue and 18th Street. It's easy to remember, because Lester Young's family lived right next door to the Local. As a matter of fact, from the upstairs you could get out of the window...and I've done it, to hop across to the roof of where Lester lived. He and I were good friends, too. This was after he'd gotten out of the Army, and I guess he never did get over the depression that that Army scene caused him.
